department: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Loans for small income-generating activities with project/unit cost up to ₹1.40 lakh for eligible Scheduled Caste applicants.
other_conditions: Individual applicant must belong to Scheduled Caste community. Partnership Firms and Co-operative Societies are also eligible, subject to all members belonging to SC and each member's annual family income not exceeding ₹3 lakh.
benefits_summary: Loan up to 90% of project cost, maximum ₹1.25 lakh per unit. Project/unit cost up to ₹1.40 lakh. Beneficiary interest rate 6.5% p.a. Repayment in quarterly instalments within maximum 3 years, including 3-month moratorium.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through authorised State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) or other Channelizing Agencies (CAs), including RRBs, Public Sector Banks and NBFC-MFIs. Applications are scrutinized by the SCA/CA, appraised and processed through the respective agency and NSFDC before disbursement.
documents_required: Passport-size photograph; Aadhaar Card; Income Certificate; Caste Certificate; Residence Proof; Bank Passbook/Bank Details; any other documents as required.
notes: Annual family income limit is ₹3 lakh in rural and urban areas, effective from 08-03-2018 according to the myScheme details. Eligibility verification is the responsibility of SCAs/CAs, with NSFDC retaining the right to re-verify.

department: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Prompt and need-based micro finance for eligible Scheduled Caste persons through selected NBFC-MFIs to pursue small or micro business activities.
other_conditions: Applicant must be an eligible Scheduled Caste person. Financial assistance is provided through selected NBFC-MFIs for pursuing small or micro business activities.
benefits_summary: NSFDC provides loan up to 90% of the project cost, with a maximum loan amount of ₹1.25 lakh for projects costing up to ₹1.40 lakh. NSFDC charges 5% interest from NBFC-MFIs, which in turn charge 15% interest from beneficiaries. The loan is repaid in quarterly instalments within a maximum period of three years, including a 3-month moratorium period.
application_process_summary: Applicants obtain financial assistance through selected NBFC-MFIs associated with NSFDC. The loan is routed through the NBFC-MFI rather than being provided directly by NSFDC to the beneficiary.
notes: Official NSFDC source confirms the loan limit, project cost, interest rate and repayment period. The provided sources do not specify age, gender, annual income ceiling or document requirements for AMY, so these fields are not assumed.

department: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Term loans for income-generating units costing more than ₹1.40 lakh and up to ₹50 lakh for eligible Scheduled Caste beneficiaries.
other_conditions: The unit/project cost must be more than ₹1.40 lakh and up to ₹50 lakh. NSFDC provides assistance through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) and Channelizing Agencies (CAs).
benefits_summary: Term loan assistance up to 90% of the project cost, with a maximum loan amount of more than ₹1.25 lakh and up to ₹45 lakh per unit. The project/unit cost must be more than ₹1.40 lakh and up to ₹50 lakh. Beneficiary interest rate is 8% p.a. Repayment is through quarterly instalments within a maximum period of seven years, including a 6-month moratorium, or 12 months for plantation and construction activities.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through authorised State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) or Channelizing Agencies (CAs). The agencies scrutinize and appraise the project proposal before forwarding eligible proposals for further processing and sanction by NSFDC.
notes: NSFDC and DoSJE sources confirm the same Term Loan parameters. Project/unit cost is more than ₹1.40 lakh and up to ₹50 lakh; maximum NSFDC loan is more than ₹1.25 lakh and up to ₹45 lakh. Interest charged to beneficiaries is 8% p.a. Repayment is within seven years with a 6-month moratorium, extended to 12 months for plantation and construction activities.

department: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Financial assistance for small and micro activities through Cooperative Societies, Cooperative Banks, and Small Finance Banks.
other_conditions: Loans are provided through Cooperative Societies, Cooperative Banks, and Small Finance Banks (SFBs) to pursue small or micro activities.
benefits_summary: Loans are provided for projects/units costing up to ₹5 lakh. NSFDC provides up to 90% of the project cost, with a maximum loan of ₹4.50 lakh. Beneficiary interest rate is 13% through Cooperative Banks/Societies and 15% through Small Finance Banks. Repayment is through quarterly or half-yearly instalments within a maximum period of 5 years, including a 3-month moratorium.
application_process_summary: Applicants obtain loans through Cooperative Societies, Cooperative Banks, and Small Finance Banks (SFBs).
notes: Official NSFDC source specifies maximum project cost of ₹5 lakh, maximum loan of ₹4.50 lakh, beneficiary interest rates of 13% through Cooperative Banks/Societies and 15% through Small Finance Banks, and repayment up to 5 years with a 3-month moratorium. Age, income, occupation, disability and document requirements are not specified in the provided source.

department: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Educational loans for eligible Scheduled Caste students pursuing regular full-time professional or technical courses in recognized institutions in India or abroad.
other_conditions: The applicant should be an eligible Scheduled Caste student pursuing a regular full-time professional or technical course approved/recognized by the Government in India or abroad. Courses must be pursued in recognized institutions. Higher education including M.Phil/PhD from recognized institutions is covered.
benefits_summary: Educational loan up to ₹40 lakh or 90% of the course fee, whichever is less. Beneficiary interest rate is 6.5% p.a. For loans where repayment has not started, repayment period is up to 12 years and moratorium is course period plus 1 year. Where repayment has started, repayment period is up to 10 years and moratorium is up to 6 months.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the District Office of the State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs). The application is scrutinized by the SCA/CA, forwarded to its Head Office, examined and recommended for sanction, then appraised by NSFDC and processed for sanction. After acceptance of sanction terms and fulfilment of required norms, NSFDC disburses funds to the SCA/CA/authorised channel partner, which then disburses the loan to the beneficiary.
documents_required: Passport-size photograph; Aadhaar Card; Income Certificate; Caste Certificate; Residence Proof; Valid Passport for study abroad; Valid Visa/Permit if applicable for study abroad; Educational Qualification Certificates; Admission Confirmation from educational institute with yearly fee and other charges payment schedule; Institute Identity Card if admission has already taken; Any other documents as required.
notes: Applicant must be a Scheduled Caste student pursuing a regular full-time Professional or Technical course in a recognized institution in India or abroad. Annual family income must be less than ₹3 lakh in rural and urban areas. Education loan is provided as one-time assistance. Study-abroad applicants require valid passport and visa/permit where applicable.

scheme_name: Credit Enhancement Guarantee Scheme for Scheduled Castes (CEGSSC)
department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment / IFCI Ltd.
short_description: Credit guarantee support for eligible Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs to facilitate access to working capital, term loans or composite term loans through Member Lending Institutions.
other_conditions: The enterprise must be promoted/run by Scheduled Caste entrepreneurs. Registered companies, registered partnership firms and registered societies must have more than 51% Scheduled Caste shareholding/membership with management control for at least the past 6 months. Sole proprietorship firms and individual SC entrepreneurs are eligible. SC promoters/partners/members must not dilute their stake below 51% during the currency of the loan. The credit facility must be without collateral security and/or third-party guarantee and must satisfy the scheme's eligibility conditions.
benefits_summary: Credit guarantee cover is available for working capital loans, term loans and composite term loans. Individual SC entrepreneurs are eligible for guarantee cover on loan amounts up to ₹1 crore. The scheme provides guarantee cover according to the sanctioned loan amount: 100% for ₹0.15–₹1 crore, 80% for ₹1–₹2 crore, 70% for ₹2–₹5 crore and 60% for amounts above ₹5 crore, subject to the applicable maximum guarantee cover. The maximum guarantee amount under the scheme is ₹5 crore. Guarantee tenure is up to 7 years or the repayment period, whichever is earlier.
application_process_summary: The entrepreneur approaches a Member Lending Institution (MLI) for the required credit facility. The MLI evaluates and sanctions the loan using its normal banking due diligence. After agreeing in principle to extend the loan, the MLI registers the loan application with IFCI for guarantee coverage and receives an acknowledgement number. The MLI submits the sanction letter, proof of disbursement and applicable guarantee fee to IFCI, after which the guarantee is issued subject to scheme conditions.
documents_required: Documentary proof of Scheduled Caste status is mandatory for the entrepreneurs, promoters, partners, society members, sole proprietorship firms or individual SC entrepreneur at the time of submitting the proposal. Other loan and business documents may be required by the concerned Member Lending Institution.
notes: CEGSSC is a credit guarantee scheme rather than a direct loan scheme. IFCI provides guarantee cover to Member Lending Institutions financing eligible SC entrepreneurs. Covered facilities include working capital loans, term loans and composite term loans. Individual SC entrepreneurs can receive guarantee cover for loan amounts up to ₹1 crore, while the overall maximum guarantee cover under the scheme is ₹5 crore. No collateral security and/or third-party guarantee is permitted for the covered credit facility. Income and age limits are not specified in the provided guidelines.

scheme_name: Vocational Education and Training Loan Scheme
department: National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Financial assistance to eligible youth of the NSKFDC target group for pursuing vocational education and training courses to improve skills, employability and self-reliance.
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to the NSKFDC target group and must have secured admission in an eligible vocational education or training course. The course must be run or supported by a Government Ministry, Department or Organisation, or by an organisation supported by NSDC or State Skill Missions/State Skill Corporations. Course duration must be a minimum of 6 months and up to 2 years and should preferably lead to a recognized Certificate, Diploma or Degree. Candidate must attain at least 18 years of age on completion of the course.
benefits_summary: Need-based finance up to 90% of course expenses, subject to a maximum loan of ₹4 lakh for courses of duration up to 2 years. Interest charged to the Channelizing Agency is 1% p.a., while beneficiaries are charged 4% p.a. Women receive an interest rebate of 0.5%. Repayment period is up to 7 years. Any cost overrun is borne by the beneficiary.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply online through the official NSKFDC website. They access the How to Apply section, open the Loan Application Form, fill in the required details and save the application form.
documents_required: Aadhaar Card; Driving License; Bank Details; Caste Certificate; Income Certificate; Domicile Certificate
notes: Course duration must be between 6 months and 2 years. Maximum loan is ₹4 lakh for courses up to 2 years and assistance covers up to 90% of course expenses. Beneficiary interest rate is 4% p.a., with a 0.5% rebate for women. Repayment is up to 7 years. Upper age limit is 50 years and candidate must attain minimum age of 18 years on completion of the course. Income ceiling is not specified in the provided source.

department: National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Financial assistance in the form of loans for income-generating activities that can mitigate the impacts of climate change, including battery electric vehicles, compressed air vehicles, solar energy gadgets and poly houses.
other_conditions: Safai Karamcharis, Scavengers and their Dependents are eligible. The activities should be income-generating and should mitigate the Green House effect or be classified as climate-change adaptation initiatives. Indicative activities include Battery Electric Vehicles (E-rickshaws), Compressed Air Vehicles, Solar Energy Gadgets and Poly Houses.
benefits_summary: Need-based loans are provided for eligible green income-generating activities. The source states an initial quantum of 90% of unit cost with a maximum of ₹2 lakh, while the benefits table specifies loan limits of ₹6.75 lakh for unit costs up to ₹7.50 lakh, ₹13.50 lakh for unit costs above ₹7.50 lakh and up to ₹15 lakh, and ₹27 lakh for unit costs above ₹15 lakh and up to ₹30 lakh. Interest rates to beneficiaries are 4%, 6% and 7% respectively. Repayment is through quarterly instalments within a maximum period of 10 years including a 6-month moratorium. Promoter contribution is 10% of unit cost.
application_process_summary: Beneficiaries submit loan applications to District Offices of State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs), branches of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), and Nationalised Banks. Applications are scrutinized and forwarded to the respective Head Offices. The viability of project proposals is appraised by the SCAs/RRBs/Nationalised Banks and viable proposals are sent to the concerned corporation along with recommendations.
documents_required: Aadhaar Card; Driving License; Bank Details; Caste Certificate; Income Certificate; Domicile Certificate
notes: Source contains inconsistencies requiring verification before final production use. The description identifies the scheme as launched by NSFDC, while the eligibility and application sections refer to NSKFDC, Safai Karamcharis, Scavengers and their Dependents, and NSKFDC channelising agencies. The source also states a maximum loan of ₹2 lakh in the initial quantum section, while the benefits table specifies maximum loan limits of ₹6.75 lakh, ₹13.50 lakh and ₹27 lakh for different unit-cost ranges up to ₹30 lakh. Interest rates are 4%, 6% and 7% for beneficiaries under the respective ranges. Verify the latest official scheme document before marking the scheme as Verified.

department: National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Microfinance assistance for women from low-income families and notified backward classes to start businesses or pursue income-generating activities, including support through Self-Help Groups (SHGs).
other_conditions: Applicant must be a woman aged 18 to 55 years. Applicant should belong to a low-income family or SC/ST/OBC category as notified by the Central/State Government, with annual family income below ₹3 lakh. The applicant should be looking to start a business or engage in income-generating activities. The scheme may provide assistance directly or through Self-Help Groups (SHGs).
benefits_summary: Microfinance assistance up to ₹1.40 lakh is provided. The scheme provides a rebate in interest for women beneficiaries. Loans are repaid within 3.5 years in quarterly instalments from the date of each disbursement, including the moratorium period. Eligible beneficiaries who repay loans under MSY through the concerned SCA can subsequently avail of loans under NSFDC schemes.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through NSFDC or the relevant State Government portal and submit the required application form and documents. Applications are processed through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) or other authorised Channelizing Agencies such as Regional Rural Banks, Public Sector Banks and NBFC-MFIs. The agencies scrutinize and forward eligible applications for further processing, sanction and disbursement.
documents_required: Address Proof; Identity Proof; SHG Membership ID; Caste Certificate if applicable; Income Certificate from a competent authority; Aadhaar Card; Bank Account Details; Recent Passport-size Photographs
notes: Source describes MSY as a women-focused microfinance scheme under NBCFDC. Eligibility states women aged 18–55 with annual family income below ₹3 lakh, including women from SC/ST/OBC categories as notified by the Central/State Government. The source also refers to low-income women and SHGs. The provided source does not specify the exact interest rate or promoter contribution. Verify the current official scheme details before final production use.

department: National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Term loan assistance for women from notified backward classes to promote self-reliance and income-generating activities.
other_conditions: Only women belonging to backward classes notified by the Central or State Governments are eligible. For projects up to ₹2 lakh, female beneficiaries are not required to make any investment. The scheme is provided under the term loan scheme.
benefits_summary: Maximum loan of ₹2 lakh per beneficiary. For projects up to ₹2 lakh, female beneficiaries are not required to invest any money. NBCFDC provides 95% of the financing and the Channel Partner provides 5%. NBCFDC charges 2% p.a. to the Channel Partner, which charges 5% p.a. to the beneficiary. Repayment is through quarterly instalments over a maximum period of 8 years, including a 6-month moratorium on recovery of principal.
application_process_summary: The provided source does not specify a detailed application process. It directs applicants to contact NBCFDC through its toll-free number or website for more information.
documents_required: Address Proof; Identity Proof; SHG Membership ID; Caste Certificate (if applicable); Income Certificate from a competent authority; Aadhaar Card; Bank Account Details; Recent Passport-size Photographs
notes: Annual family income eligibility range is ₹1,00,000 to ₹3,00,000. Applicants with annual family income below ₹1,00,000 or above ₹3,00,000 should not be considered eligible under this income criterion. The scheme is exclusively for women belonging to notified backward classes. Maximum loan is ₹2 lakh per beneficiary, with no beneficiary contribution required for projects up to ₹2 lakh. Beneficiary interest rate is 5% p.a. and repayment is over a maximum period of 8 years including a 6-month moratorium on principal repayment.

department: National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Loan assistance to eligible members of Backward Classes for income-generating activities including agriculture and allied activities, small business, artisan and traditional occupations, transport, service sector activities, and technical and professional trades or courses.
business_type: Agriculture and allied activities; Small business; Artisan and traditional occupations; Transport sector; Service sector; Technical and professional trades/courses
other_conditions: Applicant must be an entrepreneur and a member of Backward Classes as notified by the Central or State Government. Annual family income should be up to ₹3,00,000. Landless agricultural labourers and marginalized farmers with less than 1 hectare land holding belonging to Backward Classes are deemed to have annual family income below ₹1.50 lakh. Small farmers with land holdings between 1 and 2 hectares belonging to Backward Classes are deemed to have annual family income below ₹3 lakh.
benefits_summary: Loan assistance up to ₹15 lakh for eligible income-generating activities. NBCFDC finances up to 85% of the project cost and the remaining 15% is contributed by the Channel Partner and/or beneficiary. Concessional interest rates range from 6% to 8% per annum depending on the loan amount. Repayment is through quarterly instalments over a maximum period of 8 years, including a 6-month moratorium on recovery of principal.
application_process_summary: Applicants obtain the prescribed application form from the District Office of the concerned Channel Partner, which may include State Channelising Agencies (SCAs), Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), or Public Sector Banks (PSBs). The applicant fills in the required details including the proposed income-generating activity, vocational choice and training requirements, if any, and submits the completed form to the District Office of the concerned Channel Partner in the area where the applicant normally resides. The application is processed by the Channel Partner as per NBCFDC guidelines.
documents_required: Proof of Identity (Aadhaar Card); Relevant Caste Certificate issued by the relevant authority of District Administration; Passport-size Photograph; Income Certificate issued by Competent Authority of State Government/District Administration or Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) Card or Below Poverty Line (BPL) Card; Annual family income self-certification endorsed by a Gazetted Officer where applicable; Self-certification assessed and endorsed by the Branch Manager where the loan is applied through a Bank Channel Partner; Domicile Certificate
notes: Annual family income ceiling is ₹3 lakh. Landless agricultural labourers and marginalized farmers with less than 1 hectare land holding are deemed to have annual family income below ₹1.50 lakh. Small farmers with 1 to 2 hectares land holding are deemed to have annual family income below ₹3 lakh. NBCFDC finances 85% of project cost and 15% is contributed by the Channel Partner and/or beneficiary. Maximum loan is ₹15 lakh and beneficiary interest ranges from 6% to 8% depending on loan amount. Age and disability criteria are not specified in the provided source.

department: National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Education loan assistance to eligible students from Backward Classes for professional, technical and vocational education at graduate and higher levels in India or abroad.
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to Backward Classes as notified by the Central or State Government. Annual family income should be ₹3 lakh. Channel Partners are requested to release at least 50% of total funding to persons with annual family income up to ₹1.50 lakh. For professional/technical courses, the applicant must have secured admission in an approved course at a duly accredited/recognized institute and must have obtained at least 50% marks in the qualifying examination. Admission in India or abroad must be through entrance test or merit-based selection. Vocational courses must have a duration of at least 6 months and be run or supported by a Government Ministry/Department/Organisation, NSDC-supported organisation, State Skill Mission/Corporation or approved Sector Skill Council, preferably leading to a Certificate, Diploma or Degree.
benefits_summary: For professional/technical courses in India, finance is up to 90% of course expenditure subject to a maximum loan of ₹15 lakh per student. For professional/technical courses abroad, finance is up to 85% of course expenditure subject to a maximum loan of ₹20 lakh per student. For vocational courses, need-based finance covers 90% of admissible expenses subject to the prescribed limits. Covered expenses include admission and tuition fees, books, stationery and required instruments, examination fees, boarding and lodging expenses, and insurance premium during the loan period. Interest is 4% p.a. for boys and 3.5% p.a. for girls.
application_process_summary: The provided source does not specify a detailed step-by-step application process. Loans are provided through Channel Partners including State Channelising Agencies and Banks.
notes: Income ceiling is ₹3 lakh annually, with Channel Partners requested to allocate at least 50% of total funding to applicants with family income up to ₹1.50 lakh. Professional/technical course loan limit is ₹15 lakh for study in India and ₹20 lakh for study abroad. India study financing is up to 90% of course expenditure, while abroad financing is up to 85%. Beneficiary interest is 4% p.a. for boys and 3.5% p.a. for girls. The moratorium for recovery from Channel Partners is 5 years. Maximum recovery period is 10 years after the 5-year moratorium, making the total period up to 15 years from disbursement to the Channel Partner. Borrowers can prepay after repayment begins without pre-closure charges. Age, disability and specific document requirements are not specified in the provided source.

department: National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Interest subvention for OBC individuals and Self Help Groups with OBC members who have taken loans for income-generating activities from lending institutions that have signed an MoA with NBCFDC.
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to a Backward Class as notified by the Central or State Government. Annual family income must be less than ₹3 lakh. SHGs must be registered with NRLM, NULM or NABARD and have more than two years of credit history. SHGs and individuals must have made all loan repayments on time to qualify for interest subvention. OBC Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) card holders and OBC individuals facing three or more deprivations under SECC-2011, as per relevant BDO records, are eligible. OBC beneficiaries engaged in agricultural activities and covered under PM-KISAN are also eligible.
benefits_summary: Interest subvention of up to 5% per annum. Maximum loan limit is ₹4 lakh for SHGs and ₹2 lakh for individuals. The subvention amount is transferred directly into the operating account of the eligible SHG or individual.
application_process_summary: The scheme provides interest subvention on loans taken from Lending Institutions that have signed an MoA with NBCFDC. The eligible subvention amount is transferred directly into the operating account of the SHG or individual.
notes: VISVAS is an interest subvention scheme for OBC individuals and eligible OBC Self Help Groups. Annual family income must be less than ₹3 lakh. Maximum loan limit is ₹2 lakh for individuals and ₹4 lakh for SHGs, with interest subvention of up to 5% p.a. SHGs must be registered with NRLM/NULM/NABARD and have more than two years of credit history. Timely repayment is required for eligibility. Additional eligible groups include OBC Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) card holders, OBC individuals facing three or more SECC-2011 deprivations, and OBC agricultural beneficiaries covered under PM-KISAN. The provided source states that the scheme was valid for 2020-21 at that time, with further extension dependent on impact assessment; therefore current validity should be verified before production use.

department: Ministry of Finance
short_description: Bank loan facilitation for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs to establish greenfield enterprises in manufacturing, services, trading and activities allied to agriculture.
business_type: Manufacturing; Services; Trading; Activities allied to agriculture
other_conditions: Finance is provided only for Greenfield Enterprises. If the applicant is a male, he must belong to SC or ST category. The applicant must be at least 18 years old and must not be in default to any bank or financial institution. For non-individual enterprises, at least 51% of the shareholding and controlling stake must be held by an SC/ST or Woman entrepreneur.
benefits_summary: Composite loans including term loan and working capital are available between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore. A RuPay debit card is issued for borrower convenience. The Stand-Up India portal also provides hand-holding support through agencies involved in training, skill development, mentoring, project report preparation, application filling, work shed/utility support and subsidy schemes.
application_process_summary: Applicants can approach their nearest bank branch, the Lead District Manager (LDM), or apply through the Stand-Up India portal. Online applicants register on the portal, enter business location and personal details, select SC/ST/Woman category and whether the ownership stake is 51% or higher, provide proposed business and loan details, past business experience and hand-holding requirements, and complete registration. After registration, the applicant can initiate the loan application process with the respective financial institution.
documents_required: Proof of Identity; Proof of Residence; Proof of Business Address; Proof that applicant is not a defaulter with any Bank/Financial Institution; Memorandum and Articles of Association / Partnership Deed as applicable; Assets and Liabilities Statement of promoters and guarantors with latest Income Tax Returns; Rent Agreement if premises are rented; Pollution Control Board clearance if applicable; SSI/MSME Registration if applicable; Projected Balance Sheets; Lease Deeds/Title Deeds where applicable; SC/ST category proof wherever applicable; Certificate of Incorporation establishing majority stake holding in SC/ST/Woman category
notes: The scheme targets SC/ST and women entrepreneurs. Women entrepreneurs can be eligible under the scheme irrespective of SC/ST category, while male applicants must belong to SC or ST category. Applicants must be at least 18 years old and must not be in default to any bank or financial institution. For non-individual enterprises, at least 51% of shareholding and controlling stake must be held by an SC/ST or Woman entrepreneur. No annual family income ceiling is specified in the provided source. The enterprise must be a Greenfield Enterprise.

scheme_name: National Overseas Scholarship Scheme for SC etc. Candidates
department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Financial assistance to low-income students belonging to Scheduled Castes, Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes, Landless Agricultural Labourers and Traditional Artisans for pursuing Master's Degree or Ph.D. courses abroad.
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to one of the eligible categories under the scheme. The applicant must have at least 60% marks or equivalent grade in the qualifying examination. The scheme covers Master's Degree and Ph.D. courses abroad; Bachelor's level courses are not covered. Candidates must have an unconditional offer of admission from an eligible foreign institution/university. For the first round of selection in 2026, the institution/university must be among the top 500 QS World University Rankings. Candidates already staying, studying, or having completed studies abroad using another scholarship or own funds are not eligible. The award can be given only once, and not more than two children of the same parents/guardians can receive the scholarship subject to scheme conditions. Candidates must return to India within 30 days of completing the course and stay in India for at least one year.
benefits_summary: Financial assistance for Master's Degree and Ph.D. studies abroad, including annual maintenance allowance, annual contingency allowance, tuition fees, visa fees, medical insurance premium, incidental journey and equipment allowance, and air passage as prescribed under the scheme.
application_process_summary: Online applications are submitted through the National Overseas Scholarship portal at www.nosmsje.gov.in. The selection year runs from April to March. The portal is opened for applications in April/May for the first round and September/October for the second round, subject to availability of slots. Only complete online applications are considered.
documents_required: 10th Board Certificate; Caste Certificate; Photograph; Scanned Signature; Current/Permanent Address Proof; Qualifying Degree/Provisional Certificate; Mark Sheet of Qualifying Examination; Valid Document regarding Admission in Foreign University; Income Documents of all Family Members; NOC from Employer if employed; Income Tax Return Acknowledgement or Assessment Order; Aadhaar Card. After selection: Attestation Form; Self Declaration/Undertaking regarding Total Annual Family Income; Self Declaration regarding pending case/non-conviction of offence; Passport; Bonds; Solvency Certificates; Health Certificate; Passport and VISA copies; required undertakings/declarations.
notes: Applicable from 2026-27. The scheme provides 125 fresh awards per selection year subject to availability of funds: 115 for Scheduled Castes, 6 for Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes, and 4 for Landless Agricultural Labourers and Traditional Artisans. 30% of awards are earmarked for women candidates; if adequate eligible women candidates are not available, unutilized slots may be given to suitable male candidates. The maximum age is 35 years as on the first day of April of the selection year. Gross annual family income from all sources must not exceed ₹8 lakh in the last completed financial year. For the 2026-27 selection year, FY 2025-26 income is considered. If FY 2025-26 gross annual family income exceeds ₹2.5 lakh under the Old Tax Regime or ₹3 lakh under the New Tax Regime, additional ITR and CPC intimation documentation is required; these amounts are documentation thresholds and NOT the income ceiling. Minimum qualification is 60%. The scholarship duration is up to 4 years for Ph.D. and 3 years for Master's Degree, or the sanctioned course duration, whichever is earlier.

department: National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC) / Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities
short_description: Concessional credit assistance to persons with disabilities for income-generating activities, higher education, vocational or skill development, and purchase or modification of assistive devices and equipment.
business_type: Self-Employment; Higher Education; Vocational/Skill Development; Assistive Devices
other_conditions: Applicant must be an Indian citizen with 40% or more disability as defined under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 or its amendments. The applicant must possess a Unique Disability ID (UDID) Number. Normally, the applicant must be above 18 years of age; for persons with mental retardation, the eligible age is above 14 years. The age criterion does not apply to educational loans. The loan may be used for income-generating activities, higher education after Class 12, vocational or skill development courses, or purchase, customization, retrofitting or conversion of devices, machines, equipment or vehicles to disabled-friendly mode.
benefits_summary: Concessional credit up to ₹50 lakh per beneficiary/unit. For self-employment loans, the beneficiary interest rate ranges from 5% to 9% depending on the loan amount. For home loans, the beneficiary interest rate ranges from 5% to 7%. For education loans for studies in India and abroad, the beneficiary interest rate is 4%. Women with disabilities receive a 1% interest rebate on self-employment loans up to ₹50,000, subject to the scheme conditions. Loans can cover self-employment, home, education and other eligible activities under the scheme.
application_process_summary: The applicant must submit an application in the prescribed format to the implementing agency. The implementing agency processes and sanctions the loan according to the procedure and terms and conditions prescribed by NDFDC.
documents_required: Age Certificate; Unique Disability ID (UDID) Number; Documents required by the implementing agency as per its prescribed procedure; Other documents as stipulated by NDFDC/implementing agency.
notes: The scheme is specifically for persons with disabilities having 40% or more disability and possessing a UDID Number. No annual family income ceiling is specified in the provided scheme document. The overall upper limit of concessional credit is ₹50 lakh per beneficiary/unit. Self-employment loan interest rates to PwDs are 5% for loans up to ₹50,000, 6% for loans above ₹50,000 up to ₹5 lakh, 7% for loans above ₹5 lakh up to ₹15 lakh, 8% for loans above ₹15 lakh up to ₹30 lakh, and 9% for loans above ₹30 lakh up to ₹50 lakh. Home-loan beneficiary interest rates are 5% for loans up to ₹50,000 and 6% for loans above ₹50,000 up to ₹5 lakh and 7% for loans above ₹5 lakh up to ₹50 lakh. Education loans up to ₹50 lakh carry 4% interest. Women with disabilities receive a 1% interest rebate on self-employment loans up to ₹50,000, subject to the specified conditions. Repayment for self-employment loans may be up to 10 years; education-loan repayment is as sanctioned by the implementing agency. No prepayment charges are applicable after commencement of repayment.

scheme_name: National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC)
department: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment / National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC)
short_description: Fellowship providing financial assistance to Scheduled Caste students pursuing regular full-time M.Phil. or Ph.D. research in UGC-recognized universities and institutions in India.
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to the Scheduled Caste category. The fellowship is for regular and full-time M.Phil./Ph.D. courses in UGC-recognized Universities/Research Institutions. Candidates must qualify UGC-NET-JRF or Joint CSIR-UGC-NET-JRF as applicable. Candidates who have already secured admission and qualified the NET examination are given preference. A scholar can receive only one fellowship at a time and cannot simultaneously receive another scholarship/fellowship or monetary benefit from another source, subject to the scheme conditions. Employees of Universities, Colleges, Educational Institutions and Central/State/UT Governments are excluded from availing the fellowship even if they are on study leave or extraordinary leave.
benefits_summary: Financial fellowship support for M.Phil./Ph.D. research. The fellowship rate is ₹37,000 per month for Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) for the initial two years and ₹42,000 per month for Senior Research Fellowship (SRF) for the remaining tenure. Contingency grants and HRA are also provided as per applicable guidelines. HRA rates were revised to 30%, 20% and 10% for X, Y and Z cities respectively, effective from 1 January 2024. Escort/Reader assistance is available for eligible physically and visually handicapped candidates as per scheme guidelines.
application_process_summary: Selection is based on merit in the UGC-NET-JRF or Joint CSIR-UGC-NET-JRF examination. Candidates who have already secured admission are given preference. Candidates without admission may also be selected in order of merit, subject to obtaining admission to a recognized M.Phil./Ph.D. programme within the prescribed period. SC certificate authenticity is verified by the concerned University/Institution. Results and award letters are made available through the NSFDC system.
documents_required: Scheduled Caste Certificate; Aadhaar/Aadhaar EID or other permitted identity document; UGC-NET-JRF or Joint CSIR-UGC-NET-JRF qualification details; Admission/Joining documents for M.Phil./Ph.D.; Verification-cum-Joining Report; Bank Account Details; Other documents/forms prescribed by NSFDC or the concerned University/Institution.
notes: Central Sector Scheme introduced in 2005-06. The scheme provides 2,000 new fellowships per year: 1,500 for Humanities/Social Sciences and 500 for Science. NSFDC has been the Central Nodal Agency for implementation since 01.10.2022. Fellowship is for SC students pursuing M.Phil./Ph.D. in recognized Indian institutions. The fellowship is not a loan and does not require repayment. The revised fellowship rates are ₹37,000/month for JRF for the initial two years and ₹42,000/month for SRF for the remaining tenure. The 2025 official notice revised HRA to 30%, 20% and 10% for X, Y and Z cities respectively, effective from 01.01.2024. PwD candidates belonging to SC are covered through an inclusive PwD reservation provision as per applicable norms, with minimum 40% disability for PwD concessions/benefits; disability is NOT a general eligibility requirement of the scheme. There is no income ceiling specified in the provided NFSC guidelines.

department: National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Financial assistance at concessional interest rates for Safai Karamcharis and liberated Manual Scavengers to procure and operate sanitation-related equipment and vehicles and undertake sanitation-related enterprises.
business_type: Sanitation Enterprise; Mechanized Cleaning Equipment/Vehicles; Dry Waste Collection Centre (DWCC)
other_conditions: The scheme is targeted at Safai Karamcharis and liberated Manual Scavengers. Financial assistance is available to individuals, Self Help Groups (SHGs), Joint Responsibility Groups (JRGs) and Cooperatives for sanitation-related equipment/vehicles and setting up Dry Waste Collection Centres (DWCCs). For individual beneficiaries, the maximum project cost is ₹15 lakh. For SHGs/JRGs/Cooperatives, the maximum project cost is ₹50 lakh. The scheme is implemented through Channelizing Agencies (CAs). For the ULB-oriented model, beneficiaries may be nominated by Urban Local Bodies and may receive a Work Assurance Letter for mechanized cleaning work.
benefits_summary: Concessional financial assistance for sanitation-related equipment and vehicles. Maximum project cost is ₹15 lakh for individual beneficiaries and ₹50 lakh for SHGs/JRGs/Cooperatives. The beneficiary interest rate is 6% per annum. A 1% interest rebate is available for women beneficiaries and a 0.5% rebate is available for timely repayment. The repayment period is up to 7 years.
application_process_summary: Beneficiaries apply through the concerned Channelizing Agencies (CAs). Under the ULB-oriented model, Urban Local Bodies can nominate Safai Karamcharis or dependents as beneficiaries, provide a long-term Work Assurance Letter, facilitate loans through banks, and support procurement of mechanized cleaning equipment/vehicles. Banks/SCA disburse the loan and applicable capital subsidy, after which beneficiaries procure the equipment/vehicle and commence work in coordination with the ULB.
notes: The scheme has twin objectives of promoting mechanized cleaning and providing safe and sustainable livelihood opportunities to Safai Karamcharis and liberated Manual Scavengers. Individual beneficiaries can have a maximum project cost of ₹15 lakh, while SHGs/JRGs/Cooperatives can have a maximum project cost of ₹50 lakh. The beneficiary interest rate is 6% per annum, with a 1% rebate for women beneficiaries and 0.5% rebate for timely repayment. Repayment is allowed for up to 7 years. The scheme also supports setting up Dry Waste Collection Centres (DWCCs). Under the ULB model, beneficiaries may receive long-term assured mechanized cleaning work through a Work Assurance Letter. No annual income ceiling, age limit, or disability condition is specified in the provided source.

department: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Financial assistance for economically poor Scheduled Caste women, particularly widows, divorcees, single mothers and single women, to undertake income-generating activities and improve their economic empowerment.
other_conditions: The applicant must belong to the Scheduled Castes. The applicant must belong to an economically poor family meeting the prescribed Below Poverty Line income conditions. Eligible applicants include widows, divorcees, single mothers, and single women aged above 35 years, subject to the scheme conditions. The stated application age range is 25 to 50 years. Women registered under the Widow Pension Scheme may also be eligible if they satisfy the prescribed conditions. Financial assistance is provided according to the unit cost prescribed under the applicable NSFDC scheme. Eligible beneficiaries may also be considered for NSFDC Skill Training Programme assistance.
benefits_summary: Financial assistance for income-generating activities under applicable NSFDC schemes. BPL beneficiaries may receive subsidy of ₹10,000 or 50% of the unit cost, whichever is less, under the applicable Special Central Assistance provisions. The SCA may provide 2% of the loan amount as a grant for handholding activity, subject to a maximum of ₹4,000 per unit. Beneficiaries may be eligible for further assistance for business expansion after two years subject to regular repayment.
application_process_summary: Eligible applicants apply through the concerned State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) for financial assistance under the applicable NSFDC scheme. The SCA processes the application and provides applicable margin money and assistance according to NSFDC guidelines.
notes: The provided source states rural family income up to ₹98,000 per annum and urban family income up to ₹1,20,000 per annum as the applicable Below Poverty Line limits. These are location-specific limits, so income_ceiling_annual is kept as Not Specified rather than forcing one single annual ceiling. The scheme does not specify a separate maximum loan amount; beneficiaries can avail financial assistance according to the unit cost prescribed under the applicable NSFDC scheme. NSFDC may charge 1% interest, while the SCA charges 4% to beneficiaries. Repayment is in quarterly instalments over a maximum period of 10 years, including a moratorium of 3 to 24 months depending on the nature of the scheme. The scheme specifically targets women from Scheduled Castes who meet the stated social and economic conditions.

department: National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) / Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
short_description: Financial assistance to women Safai Karamcharis, Scavengers and their dependent daughters for small and petty trade, business and other income-generating activities.
business_type: Small/Petty Trade; Business; Sundry Income-Generating Activities
other_conditions: The applicant must be a woman Safai Karamchari or Scavenger or a dependent daughter of a Safai Karamchari or Scavenger. The scheme targets economically poor beneficiaries. Loan assistance is provided through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs), Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and Nationalized Banks. Promoter's contribution is not required from beneficiaries. The remaining 10% of unit cost may be provided by the SCA through loan, subsidy or other available sources.
benefits_summary: Loan assistance up to ₹2,00,000 per beneficiary/unit. NSFDC loan component can cover up to 90% of the unit cost. Interest charged to beneficiaries is 7% per annum. No promoter contribution is required from beneficiaries. A 2% loan amount grant may be provided by the SCA for handholding activities, subject to a maximum of ₹4,000 per unit.
application_process_summary: Eligible beneficiaries apply through State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs), Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) or Nationalized Banks. The concerned implementing agency processes the loan application according to the applicable NSKFDC guidelines.
notes: Maximum project cost is ₹2,00,000 per beneficiary/unit. NSFDC can provide up to 90% of the unit cost, while the remaining 10% is provided by the SCA through loan, subsidy or other available sources. Beneficiary interest rate is 7% per annum. Repayment period is 5 years after an implementation period of 4 months and a moratorium period of 6 months. The scheme does not specify an annual income ceiling in the provided source. No age limit or disability requirement is specified in the provided source.

department: Government of Gujarat
short_description: Assistance scheme for eligible beneficiaries in Gujarat through toolkits and equipment for approved trades and income-generating activities.
other_conditions: For beneficiaries in rural areas, inclusion in the District Rural Development Department poverty-line list is required. Beneficiaries with a 0–16 score are not required to submit an income certificate. Other beneficiaries must provide an income certificate showing annual family income up to ₹6,00,000 issued by the competent authority. Applicants must apply online through the e-Kutir portal and upload the required documents including e-Shram Card details and caste certificate. For 12 extremely backward castes among Scheduled Castes and extremely backward, nomadic and denotified castes among Socially and Educationally Backward Classes, no income limit applies and only the caste certificate is required.
benefits_summary: Eligible beneficiaries receive financial assistance through approved toolkits/equipment for eligible trades. An e-voucher with a QR code is generated after approval, which can be redeemed through authorized dealers in Gujarat. Applicants may also opt for training through the portal. The toolkit can be purchased up to the maximum approved value, with any excess cost borne by the beneficiary.
application_process_summary: Applicants must apply online through the e-Kutir portal at https://e-kutir.gujarat.gov.in. Required documents must be uploaded online, including e-Shram Card details and caste certificate. Applications are submitted and considered through the prescribed online selection process. After toolkit approval, an e-voucher/QR code is generated and can be redeemed through an authorized dealer. Post-purchase verification is conducted by the concerned authorities/third-party agency.
documents_required: e-Shram Card; Caste Certificate; Income Certificate where applicable; Other required documents as specified in the online application.
notes: State-specific scheme for Gujarat. Age eligibility is 18 to 60 years. Annual family income limit is ₹6,00,000 for applicable beneficiaries. Rural beneficiaries may qualify through inclusion in the District Rural Development Department poverty-line list; beneficiaries with a 0–16 poverty-line score do not need to submit an income certificate. For 12 extremely backward castes among Scheduled Castes and extremely backward, nomadic and denotified castes among Socially and Educationally Backward Classes, no income limit applies and only the caste certificate is required. Applicants must possess/provide e-Shram Card details. Toolkit assistance is provided through an e-voucher/QR code and authorized dealers. Any amount exceeding the approved maximum toolkit value must be paid by the beneficiary. Post-purchase verification is carried out, and misuse of government assistance can result in recovery of the assistance and disqualification from future government schemes.

department: Gujarat Tribal Development Department / Gujarat Tribal Development Corporation
short_description: Concessional loan assistance to unemployed Scheduled Tribe individuals residing in Gujarat for starting self-employment activities under approved business activities.
business_type: Trade; Service; Small Manufacturing; Other Approved Self-Employment Activities
other_conditions: The applicant must be a resident of Gujarat and belong to the Scheduled Tribe (ST) category. The applicant must be unemployed at the time of applying. The proposed activity must be one of the approved business activities under the scheme.
benefits_summary: Loan assistance ranging from ₹50,000 to ₹5,00,000 at an interest rate of 4% per annum for eligible self-employment activities.
application_process_summary: Applicants can apply through the Gujarat Tribal Development Corporation's prescribed application process. The applicant provides personal, category and business-related information and submits the required documents for processing by the concerned authority.
documents_required: Aadhaar Card; Caste Certificate; Income Certificate; Ration Card; Business Address Proof; Identity Card; Artisan Identity Card if applicable; Passport-size Photographs; Age Proof; Bank Passbook or Cancelled Cheque; Affidavit; Quotations; 7/12 Certificate where applicable.
notes: Gujarat-specific ST self-employment scheme. The myScheme information states that loan assistance ranges from ₹50,000 to ₹5,00,000 at 4% annual interest and covers approved self-employment activities. The applicant must belong to the Scheduled Tribe category and be unemployed. The current income ceiling, age criteria and other detailed conditions require verification from the latest official Gujarat Tribal Development Corporation notification. An older Gujarat government publication contains different income-related information, so the income ceiling is kept as Not Specified until the current official notification is confirmed.

department: Social Justice and Empowerment Department, Gujarat / Dr. Ambedkar Antyodaya Development Corporation
short_description: Loan assistance to unemployed individuals belonging to Scheduled Caste Antyodaya families in Gujarat for purchasing passenger or freight vehicles to create self-employment opportunities in the transport sector.
business_type: Transport Sector; Passenger Vehicle; Freight/Loading Vehicle
other_conditions: Applicant must be a resident of Gujarat, belong to the Scheduled Caste (SC) category, be unemployed, and belong to an Antyodaya family. Annual family income must not exceed ₹3,00,000.
benefits_summary: Financial assistance in the form of a loan for purchasing passenger or freight/loading vehicles to create self-employment opportunities in the transport sector. The provided source does not specify the maximum loan amount or interest rate.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply online through the Dr. Ambedkar Antyodaya Development Corporation (DAADC) online portal. The applicant must register or log in, fill in the application form with personal and scheme-specific details, upload the required documents, and submit the application.
documents_required: Aadhaar Card; Ration Card; First Page of Bank Passbook; Income Certificate; Caste Certificate; Abstract of Driving Licence; School Leaving Certificate / Birth Certificate / Medical Officer or Civil Surgeon Certificate; Driving Licence
notes: Gujarat-specific SC self-employment scheme targeted specifically at unemployed members of Scheduled Caste Antyodaya families. Annual family income ceiling is ₹3 lakh. The scheme supports purchase of passenger or freight/loading vehicles for transport-sector self-employment. The provided source does not specify age eligibility, disability eligibility, maximum loan amount, interest rate, repayment period, or beneficiary contribution; these details should not be assumed and require verification from the latest official DAADC scheme guidelines.

department: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME)
short_description: A credit-linked subsidy programme supporting new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector to generate self-employment and sustainable employment in rural and urban areas.

scheme_name: D Devaraj Urs Individual Loan Scheme
department: D Devaraj Urs Backward Classes Development Corporation (KSBCDC) / Department of Backward Classes Welfare, Govt of Karnataka
short_description: Financial assistance for self-employment activities under business, service, and agricultural and allied activities for Backward Class persons in Karnataka.
business_type: Business / Service / Agriculture and allied activities
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to a Backward Class category recognized in Karnataka.
benefits_summary: Financial assistance up to ₹50,000 per beneficiary. The amount includes 30% (maximum ₹10,000) as subsidy and the remaining as loan at 4% interest per annum.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the District Office of D Devaraj Urs Backward Classes Development Corporation (Devaraja Arasu Bhavan) or via the Corporation's Suvidha portal.
notes: Official Karnataka government source (dbcdc.karnataka.gov.in). Age, income ceiling and document requirements beyond 'Backward Class' membership are not specified in the provided source.

department: D Devaraj Urs Backward Classes Development Corporation (KSBCDC) / Department of Backward Classes Welfare, Govt of Karnataka
short_description: Education loan for Backward Class students in Karnataka studying Medical, Engineering and other professional courses.
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to a Backward Class category and be studying Medical, Engineering or another professional course. Annual family income should not exceed ₹3.50 lakh.
benefits_summary: Loan of ₹1 lakh per year or actual cost incurred towards admission fee, tuition fee, laboratory fee, examination fee etc., whichever is applicable. Interest rate is 2% per annum.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the Corporation's Suvidha portal / District Office.
notes: Official Karnataka government source. Age and specific document list not specified in the provided source.

scheme_name: Interest Free Loan for Higher Education in Foreign University
department: D Devaraj Urs Backward Classes Development Corporation (KSBCDC) / Department of Backward Classes Welfare, Govt of Karnataka
short_description: Interest-free loan for Backward Class (Category-1, 2A, 3A, 3B) students in Karnataka pursuing Master's Degree or Ph.D. at top-ranked foreign universities.
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to Backward Classes Category-1, 2A, 3A or 3B. Admitting foreign university must be ranked below 1000 in QS World Rankings. Minimum 60% marks required in qualifying examination. Annual family income should not exceed ₹15 lakh.
benefits_summary: Maximum loan of ₹50 lakh over 2 years (up to ₹25 lakh per year), interest-free.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the Corporation's Suvidha portal / District Office.
notes: Official Karnataka government source, but the page text appears machine-translated/garbled regarding exact age criteria (references both '32 years for Master's/PhD' and a '35 year' limit). Verify precise age criteria against the original Kannada notification before production use.

department: Karnataka State Women's Development Corporation (KSWDC) / Department of Women and Child Development, Govt of Karnataka
short_description: Women entrepreneurship scheme providing subsidised loans to women for starting or expanding small-scale businesses in trade and service sectors.
other_conditions: Applicant must be a woman seeking to start or expand a small-scale trade or service business. Category-based subsidy rates apply.
benefits_summary: Subsidised loans up to ₹3 lakh. SC/ST women, widows and women with disabilities receive a 50% subsidy up to ₹1.5 lakh; women in general/other special categories receive a 30% subsidy up to ₹90,000.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through KSWDC or partner bank branches.
notes: Detailed figures sourced from a secondary aggregator (niir.org) summarising the scheme rather than a primary KSWDC document directly fetched; a myScheme listing exists (URL given) but its detailed content could not be retrieved directly in this session. Age and income-ceiling criteria are not confirmed and should be verified against KSWDC's official scheme document before production use.

department: Tamil Nadu Adi Dravidar Housing and Development Corporation (TAHDCO) / Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department
short_description: Bank loans arranged with TAHDCO subsidy for self-employment of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe individuals (including SC converts to Christianity) in Tamil Nadu.
business_type: Petrol/Diesel/Gas retail; general small business (financed via banks under MUDRA/Stand-Up India)
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe (including SC converted to Christianity) and be an unemployed entrepreneur aged 18-65. Annual family income should be below ₹3 lakh (some district sources state ₹1 lakh for specific sub-categories).
benefits_summary: Banks sanction loans (including via MUDRA/Stand-Up India) and TAHDCO releases a subsidy. For setting up Petrol/Diesel/Gas retail outlets, subsidy is 30% of project cost up to a maximum of ₹2.25 lakh.
application_process_summary: Applicants approach banks directly or apply through the TAHDCO District Manager's office; TAHDCO releases the subsidy component once the bank sanctions the loan.
notes: Official district-level TAHDCO pages. Income ceiling is stated as ₹3 lakh in most district sources (Ariyalur, Thanjavur) but one source (Viluppuram) cites ₹1 lakh for a related women-specific sub-scheme; treat ₹3 lakh as the general EDP ceiling.

scheme_name: Economic Assistance to Self Help Groups (EA to SHG)
department: Tamil Nadu Adi Dravidar Housing and Development Corporation (TAHDCO) / Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department
short_description: Credit assistance to Adi Dravidar (Scheduled Caste) women's Self Help Groups in Tamil Nadu for income-generating economic activities.
other_conditions: SHG members must belong to Scheduled Caste. Annual family income of applicants should not exceed ₹3 lakh. SHGs must have been accredited (graded) at least twice to access the income-generating loan component.
benefits_summary: Credit for income-generating activities up to ₹2.5 lakh or 50% of the project cost, whichever is lower, at a reasonable interest rate. A one-time Front-End Subsidy of ₹25,000 per SHG is also available for revolving fund.
application_process_summary: SHGs apply through the TAHDCO District Manager's office.
notes: Official district TAHDCO pages. This is distinct from the general EDP scheme and specifically targets registered women's SHGs.

department: Tamil Nadu Adi Dravidar Housing and Development Corporation (TAHDCO) / Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department
short_description: Subsidy assistance to Scheduled Caste women in Tamil Nadu to purchase and develop agricultural land, improving their land holding and socio-economic status.
other_conditions: Applicant must be a Scheduled Caste woman aged 18-65. Annual family income should not exceed ₹1 lakh (per one district source; other TAHDCO income ceilings for related schemes are stated as ₹3 lakh, so this should be re-confirmed). Applicant and family must not have availed any prior subsidy under TAHDCO schemes.
benefits_summary: Subsidy of a maximum of 30% of the project cost or ₹2.25 lakh, whichever is less, released as Front-End subsidy. 100% stamp duty exemption is provided for registration of the land purchased under the scheme.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the TAHDCO District Manager's office.
notes: Income ceiling for this specific land-purchase sub-scheme (₹1 lakh) differs from the ₹3 lakh ceiling cited for other TAHDCO schemes in other district sources; verify the current applicable ceiling with TAHDCO head office before production use.

department: District Industries Centres (DIC) / Directorate of Industries, Government of Maharashtra
short_description: Soft loan (seed money) to unemployed persons in Maharashtra to meet part of the margin money required to avail institutional finance for self-employment ventures in industry, service and business.
other_conditions: Applicant must be an unemployed person proposing a project approved by a financial institution/bank. Project cost limit is ₹25 lakh for industry, service and business activities.
benefits_summary: Seed money assistance at 15% of the project cost approved by the financial institution for general category applicants. For projects up to ₹10 lakh, the quantum of assistance is increased to 20% for SC/ST/OBC/NT/VT and Handicapped applicants. Interest rate is 6% per annum, with a 3% rebate for regular, on-time repayment (net 3% effective interest). Repayment starts after 3 years in 4 yearly instalments (6 months for vehicle loans).
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the concerned District Industries Centre (DIC) after securing in-principle finance approval from a bank/financial institution.
notes: Official Maharashtra Industry, Trade and Investment Facilitation (MAITRI) portal. Age and specific documents not detailed in the provided source.

scheme_name: Margin Money Scheme for SC/ST Tiny Units
department: District Industries Centres (DIC) / Directorate of Industries, Government of Maharashtra
short_description: Margin money/subsidy assistance to Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs in Maharashtra to set up tiny units (investment in plant & machinery below ₹2 lakh) in towns and rural areas with population under 1 lakh.
business_type: Tiny units — Small Scale Industries, Village Industries, handicrafts, handlooms, silk and coir industries
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe. The unit must fall within the purview of the Small Scale Industries Board or Village Industries/handicrafts/handloom/silk/coir sectors, be located in a town/rural area with population under 1 lakh, with plant & machinery investment below ₹2 lakh.
benefits_summary: Margin Money assistance of up to 30% of total fixed capital investment or a maximum of ₹60,000, whichever is less (compared to 20% or ₹40,000 for general category applicants). Interest is 4% per annum, with 1% penal interest on default. Repayment is within 8 years with an initial moratorium of 2 years.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the concerned District Industries Centre (DIC).
notes: Sourced from the Government of Maharashtra's 'Doing Business in Maharashtra' portal listing DIC schemes. Especially useful for rural artisans per the source.

department: Other Backward Classes Development Corporation (OBCDC), Government of Maharashtra
short_description: Interest-subvention loans to Other Backward Class community members in Maharashtra for commercial and industrial self-employment ventures, with the state government bearing the interest cost.
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to an Other Backward Class community in Maharashtra proposing a commercial or industrial self-employment venture.
benefits_summary: Direct loan of up to ₹1 lakh for individual enterprising ventures. Loans disbursed via OBCDC of up to ₹10 lakh for individuals and up to ₹50 lakh for groups of individuals. The Maharashtra government pays interest of up to 12% per annum on the loan on the beneficiary's behalf, effectively making it interest-free to the borrower, subject to timely repayment.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the Other Backward Classes Development Corporation (OBCDC).
notes: Sourced from a 2019 news report on a Maharashtra state budget announcement rather than a primary OBCDC scheme document; loan limits and interest-subvention terms should be re-confirmed against the current official OBCDC scheme notification, as budget-announced limits can change year to year.

department: Rajasthan Scheduled Castes Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Cooperative Corporation Limited (RSCSTFDCCL) / Social Justice and Empowerment Department, Government of Rajasthan
short_description: Concessional-interest self-employment loan scheme for Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Other Backward Class, Safai Karamchari and disabled individuals in Rajasthan.
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Other Backward Class, be a Safai Karamchari, or a Person with Disability, and be a resident of Rajasthan seeking self-employment.
benefits_summary: Loans provided at a concessional rate of interest for self-employment purposes; exact loan amount and interest rate are not specified in the sources reviewed. Loan applications are reviewed by a division-level loan appraisal team, which approves or rejects applications within 3 months of receipt, and disbursed to the applicant's Jan Aadhaar-linked bank account.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply online during the annual application window (historically 1 September to 30 November) via the Rajasthan SSO portal (sso.rajasthan.gov.in) or through e-Mitra kiosks.
source_links: https://sso.rajasthan.gov.in/ (portal) — details compiled from secondary aggregator sources
notes: Only secondary aggregator sources (sarkariyojana.com and similar) were available in this session rather than a primary RSCSTFDCCL/Social Justice Department document; specific loan amount, interest rate, age and income-ceiling figures could not be confirmed and must be verified against the Corporation's official scheme notification before production use.

department: Kerala State Development Corporation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Ltd (KSDCSCST) / Department of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Development, Government of Kerala
short_description: Loan scheme for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe individuals in Kerala, particularly those who have undergone relevant training, to take up self-employment in agriculture, industry, trade and commerce.
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe in Kerala; preference given to those who have undergone relevant skill training.
benefits_summary: Interest rate is 7% per annum for loans up to ₹5 lakh, and 9% per annum for loans above ₹5 lakh. Repayment period is 5 years.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through KSDCSCST district/regional offices.
notes: Official Kerala government (KSDCSCST) source. Maximum loan amount, age and income-ceiling criteria are not specified in the provided source.

department: Kerala State Backward Classes Development Corporation (KSBCDC) / Department of Backward Classes Development, Government of Kerala
short_description: Loan scheme for Backward Class individuals in Kerala to take up self-employment ventures, financed through the National Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (NMDFC) channel.
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to a Backward Class/minority community as per NMDFC/KSBCDC eligibility norms.
benefits_summary: Maximum loan amount of ₹20 lakh at an interest rate of 6% per annum.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through KSBCDC district offices.
notes: Sourced from a Kerala district administration page listing KSBCDC schemes. Repayment period, age and income-ceiling criteria are not specified in the provided source.

department: Department of Social Justice, Government of Kerala
short_description: One-time financial assistance for self-employment to dependents of crime victims, or individuals seriously injured due to criminal acts, in Kerala.
other_conditions: Applicant must be either a person seriously injured in a crime, or a dependent (spouse or unmarried child) of a crime victim. Annual family income should not exceed ₹1 lakh. Application must be submitted within 5 years of the crime.
benefits_summary: One-time financial aid of ₹20,000 to initiate a self-employment activity.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the Department of Social Justice, Government of Kerala (district offices).
notes: Piloted in Pathanamthitta district in 2020 before statewide extension. Sourced via a Wikipedia article citing the Kerala Department of Social Justice site (sjd.kerala.gov.in); recommend cross-checking directly against sjd.kerala.gov.in before production use.

department: Kerala State Women's Development Corporation (KSWDC) / Department of Social Justice, Government of Kerala
short_description: Self-employment loan scheme for transgender community members in Kerala to support viable self-employment projects.
other_conditions: Applicant must be a member of the transgender community in Kerala with a viable, sustainable self-employment project proposal.
benefits_summary: Loan ranging from ₹3 lakh to ₹15 lakh. Up to 70% of the sanctioned loan is disbursed initially, with the remaining 30% released subsequently, subject to scheme conditions.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the Kerala State Women's Development Corporation (KSWDC).
notes: Sourced from a news report on the scheme's launch rather than a primary KSWDC scheme document; exact eligibility conditions, interest rate and repayment terms should be verified against KSWDC's official scheme guidelines before production use.

department: Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Castes Cooperative Finance Corporation (APSCCFC) / Social Welfare Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
short_description: Bank-linked and non-bank-linked economic support schemes for Scheduled Caste individuals in Andhra Pradesh to set up self-employment units such as small business, transport and services.
business_type: Kirana shops, tent house, fancy shop, bakery, internet centre, transport (autos, mini vans, cars) and other small businesses
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to Scheduled Caste. Eligibility is based on double the poverty line: annual family income should not exceed ₹98,000 in rural areas and ₹1,20,000 in urban areas. Special emphasis is given to vulnerable sub-groups such as Flayers & Tanners, Bonded Labour and Jogins.
benefits_summary: Unit cost is typically ₹1 lakh with subsidy support; per a 2013 policy change the subsidy component for self-employment schemes was enhanced to 60% of unit cost or ₹1 lakh, whichever is less (GO Ms.No.101, SW(SCP-1) Dept, dt. 31.12.2013), with the balance financed as a bank loan tied up by the District SC Cooperative Society.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the District SC Cooperative Society (functioning under the District Collector's chairmanship), which scrutinises and ties up the loan with banks before releasing the subsidy.
documents_required: Caste Certificate; Income Certificate; Aadhaar Card; Bank Account Details; Project/business proposal; other documents as required by the District Society.
notes: Sourced from official Andhra Pradesh district administration pages. Subsidy percentage has changed over time via government orders (60%/₹1 lakh cap per the 2013 GO cited); benefit levels should be re-confirmed against the current year's action plan (SCAP) before production use, as funding and subsidy ratios are revised periodically.

scheme_name: BC Corporation Individual Self-Employment Scheme (Margin Money / BC Abhyudaya Yojana)
department: Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Cooperative Finance Corporation (APBCCFC) / BC Welfare Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
short_description: Financial assistance to educated unemployed youth, skilled labourers and artisans from Backward Classes in Andhra Pradesh for self-employment, via Margin Money assistance in rural areas and BC Abhyudaya Yojana in urban areas.
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to a Backward Class community and be aged between 21 and 50 years, and be an educated unemployed person, skilled labourer or artisan.
benefits_summary: Financial assistance through institutional (bank) finance with a 50% subsidy as matching grant, subject to a maximum of ₹1,00,000 on the unit cost, whichever is less. Since 2016-17 the Corporation provides this as a back-end subsidy (i.e., released after the bank loan is disbursed) rather than acting as a direct lender.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the District BC/SC Society, which functions per guidelines issued by APBCCFC; the Corporation acts as a facilitator for the subsidy rather than as a direct lending agency.
notes: Official Andhra Pradesh district administration source. Income ceiling and specific documents not stated in the provided source.

scheme_name: ADARANA Programme (Toolkit Scheme for BC Artisans)
department: Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Cooperative Finance Corporation (APBCCFC) / BC Welfare Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
short_description: Toolkit and equipment assistance scheme for traditional artisans from Backward Classes in Andhra Pradesh to modernise their trade tools.
business_type: Toolkit / equipment procurement for traditional trades
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to a Backward Class traditional artisan community in Andhra Pradesh.
benefits_summary: Financial assistance in three unit-cost slabs — ₹10,000, ₹20,000 and ₹30,000 — for procurement of tools and gadgets, structured as 70% subsidy, 20% loan (via NBCFDC) and 10% beneficiary contribution. The scheme targeted 105,000 beneficiaries at the ₹10,000 slab, 83,000 at the ₹20,000 slab and 67,000 at the ₹30,000 slab in its 2018-19 relaunch. A follow-on 'ADARANA PLUS' scheme was also proposed for higher-end mechanised tools above the ₹30,000 ceiling.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the District BC Corporation / APBCCFC channel as per the ADARANA guidelines (G.O.Ms.No.1, BC Welfare Dept, dated 10-03-2018).
notes: Guidelines are from the scheme's 2018-19 relaunch (G.O.Ms.No.1 dated 10-03-2018); current year's beneficiary targets and unit-cost slabs should be verified against the latest APBCCFC/ADARANA notification (adarana.ap.gov.in) before production use.

department: Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Tribes Cooperative Finance Corporation Ltd (APSTCFC / TRICOR) / Tribal Welfare Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
short_description: Bank-linked and non-bank-linked economic support schemes for Scheduled Tribe families in Andhra Pradesh for self-employment and livelihood activities, including novel welfare schemes such as mobile dispensing units for PDS door-delivery.
business_type: Small business, transport (e.g. four-wheeler mobile dispensing units), and other income-generating activities
other_conditions: Applicant must belong to a Scheduled Tribe community in Andhra Pradesh. For specific novel schemes (e.g. mobile dispensing units for PDS delivery), candidates are shortlisted by a Screening-cum-Selection Committee headed by the MPDO/Municipal Commissioner and consolidated by the Project Officer, ITDA or District Tribal Welfare Officer (for non-ITDA areas).
benefits_summary: Economic support schemes are implemented with loan tie-up from banks and directly by the District ST Corporation, in convergence with line departments. A specific novel scheme provided 700 four-wheeler mini-truck mobile dispensing units (unit cost approximately ₹5.81 lakh) for door-delivery of PDS commodities to ST beneficiaries.
application_process_summary: Applicants apply through the District ST Corporation office or, for novel/targeted schemes, through the Project Officer, ITDA / District Tribal Welfare Officer (Non-ITDA areas), following a Screening-cum-Selection Committee process.
notes: General ST Corporation economic-support activity is well documented at the district level; the mobile dispensing unit example is one specific novel scheme (from a 2020 Government Order) rather than the Corporation's full scheme catalogue.
